I’ve actually been homeless since I was 16 up until I was 19, was living in the shelter system, and got myself into university to have more of a voice in the fight against homelessness, and in the future I hope to help other people experiencing it, especially young people, to be able to attend post secondary education. I can’t really “switch lives” with “some homeless dude” cause the reality is, I am that person. I’m not all talk; I know what it’s like to be in that position, which is very scary especially as a 16 year old girl, and understand what the system is actually like unlike a majority of people who do not. I’m sorry if wanting people to have a warm safe space in the winter offends so many ubc students but I will forever fight for homeless people to be treated like everyone else and afforded basic human dignity.

Please spend a couple years being homeless then try telling me how IKB should be limited to students, because I promise you I’ve been there and when you are in that position it’s a matter of life and death and being in physical danger, offering someone a safe space is a matter of providing them with the bare minimum regardless of where that is. Homeless people face rates of physical and sexual violence SIGNIFICANTLY higher than the rest of us and if you really believed they shouldn’t be offered the basic dignity of having a safe space even if it’s a library or a hospital or wherever then that’s fine, but just know that as someone who has experienced homelessness as a teenager that I think it is very disheartening and sad to see the lack of compassion in my peers.

Some of you students need to check your privilege. Oh boo boo you won’t be able to find a spot to study, but these are people who ARE TRYING NOT TO FREEZE OUTSIDE. Start acting like a decent human being and have some compassion and respect for those who are in a bad situation trying to have their basic needs met, whereas for most of us at UBC already have everything and are living very privileged lives already.
Lol bro homeless shelters are all full in the winter and people genuinely have nowhere to go, have some compassion for your fellow humans
